facts.statement: Ferrisaurus is a ceratopsian dinosaur found in the Sustut Basin of British Columbia, Canada.
facts.quote: Ferrisaurus is a genus of leptoceratopsid ceratopsian dinosaur from the Sustut Basin (Tango Creek Formation) in British Columbia, Canada.

facts.statement: Ferrisaurus is the first non-avian dinosaur species formally described from British Columbia.
facts.quote: It is the first non-avian dinosaur described from British Columbia.

facts.statement: Canadian geologist Kenny F. Larsen discovered Ferrisaurus fossils in 1971 while prospecting for thorium in north-central British Columbia.
facts.quote: During 1971 Canadian geologist Kenny F. Larsen discovered dinosaur remains while exploring the Sustut Basin in north-central British Columbia while prospecting for Thorium

facts.statement: The fossils were located in a radioactive talus deposit near the confluence of Birdflat Creek and the Sustut River.
facts.quote: The fossils were discovered because they were slightly radioactive, from a talus deposit along a railway cut near the confluence of Birdflat Creek and Sustut River.

facts.statement: Larsen donated the fossils to Dalhousie University in 2004, and they were later accessioned by the Royal BC Museum in 2006.
facts.quote: Larsen originally held onto the fossils until 2004, when he donated them to Dalhousie University before being accessioned by the Royal BC Museum in 2006 as RBCM.EH.2006.019.

facts.statement: The genus name Ferrisaurus translates to "iron lizard," referencing the discovery site along a railway line.
facts.quote: The genus name translates as "iron lizard" from the Latin ferrum and Ancient Greek σαῦρος (sauros) in reference to the discovery along a rail line

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ferrisaurus is nicknamed "Buster".
Fossil evidence indicates Ferrisaurus lived roughly 68.2 to 67.2 million years ago during the Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: The presumed holotype locality included a Maastrichtian marker palynomorph taxon indicating an age of roughly 68.2–67.2 million years old for Ferrisaurus, within the Tatlatui Member of the Tango Creek Formation.

facts.statement: Ferrisaurus is classified within the family Leptoceratopsidae based on phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Arbour and Evans recovered Ferrisaurus within Leptoceratopsidae with a phylogenetic analysis, though its incompleteness hindered resolution.

facts.statement: Ferrisaurus shares anatomical features such as a bent ulna and fused astragalus and tibia with other leptoceratopsids.
facts.quote: Ferrisaurus shares a bent ulna with Cerasinops and Prenoceratops, a fused astragalus and tibia with Montanoceratops, and proportions of the foot with Udanoceratops.

rejected.statement: In 2019, Arbour and Evans reidentified bones including the pectoral girdle, forearm, and lower leg to classify the specimen as a distinct leptoceratopsid named Ferrisaurus sustutensis.
rejected.quote: Arbour and Evans also reidentified multiple of the bones, instead considering that the pectoral girdle, forearm, and lower leg were present, with this reidentification allowing RBCM P900 to be given the name Ferrisaurus sustutensis as a distinct leptoceratopsid.
